entities.summary: John Hobart, 2nd Earl of Buckinghamshire was a British politician, courtier, and diplomat who played a significant role in shaping the country's relations with the Americas during the late 18th century. Born into a prominent family, Hobart was educated at Eton College and later served as a member of Parliament for the borough of Buckingham. In 1766, he was appointed as the British ambassador to the United States, a position he held until 1775. His tenure was marked by a series of diplomatic incidents, including the Boston Tea Party, which he viewed as an affront to British authority. Hobart's efforts to resolve the crisis ultimately failed, but his experience in the role contributed to his later success as a diplomat in Europe. After leaving office, he returned to England and continued to serve in Parliament until his death in 1793. Hobart's legacy is complex, reflecting both his commitment to British interests and his recognition of the need for greater cooperation with its American colonies.
